stewards.name: x402 Foundation (x402 a Series of LF Projects, LLC)
stewards.role: Governs the protocol under a technical charter adopted 2026-03-31, as a Linux Foundation project announced on 2026-04-02. A Governing Board handles budget and business oversight and the TSC makes technical decisions; Michael Hursta (Linux Foundation) has been Executive Director since 2026-10-01.

stewards.name: Technical Steering Committee: Coinbase, Cloudflare, Stripe
stewards.role: Votes on technical decisions; named in TSC.md on 2026-05-12.

stewards.name: Coinbase Developer Platform
stewards.role: Originated x402 and wrote the 2025-05-06 whitepaper; runs the largest facilitator by transactions and volume in x402scan figures reported on 2026-07-21.

implementers.name: Coinbase CDP facilitator
implementers.role: Facilitator on Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, Monad, World and Solana with KYT and OFAC screening (CDP docs, 2026-10-19).

implementers.name: Facilitators listed in the x402 docs (PayAI, Corbits, Dexter, Fireblocks, Polygon, Celo, NEAR x402 Facilitator, T54 XRPL and others)
implementers.role: Independent verify and settle services; the docs say the list is not exhaustive.

implementers.name: Tempo x402 facilitator
implementers.role: Facilitator at api.tempo.xyz/v1/x402 since 2026-11-19: buyers pay USDC on Base mainnet with exact to Tempo's deposit address, which the public GET /supported publishes, and Tempo pays the seller in OUSD on Tempo mainnet at the address named in extra.tempoSettlement; sellers need an API key with the mpp:write scope. The buyer's signed payTo is Tempo's address, so the seller relies on Tempo for the payout.

implementers.name: Cloudflare Monetization Gateway
implementers.role: Closed beta that settles USDC on Base through Coinbase's facilitator; US sellers and buyers only.

implementers.name: Cloudflare Agents SDK
implementers.role: withX402 and paidTool for agents and MCP servers since 2025-09-23.

implementers.name: Cloudflare AI Gateway machine payments
implementers.role: Pays for inference on select models over x402 when a request carries the Cloudflare-specific Payment-Method: x402 header; since 2026-09-30, for US-based customers.

implementers.name: AWS WAF AI traffic monetization (Amazon CloudFront)
implementers.role: Seller side at the edge since 2026-06-15: a Monetize rule on a web ACL for a CloudFront distribution answers AI bots and agents with an x402 402 (a USDC price, Base and Solana, the publisher's payTo), verifies the payment at the edge and settles it through Coinbase Developer Platform's x402 facilitator after a successful origin fetch. Prices can differ by verification tier, Web Bot Auth included, and AWS takes no fee on content revenue. Stripe direct-account payments and MPP were announced as coming soon; the WAF guide read 2026-11-21 names only x402.

implementers.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments
implementers.role: Buyer side, managed payments for agents. Announced in preview on 2026-05-07, it pays x402 from Coinbase CDP or Stripe Privy wallets within session spending limits, with the Coinbase x402 Bazaar MCP server reachable through AgentCore Gateway. General availability on 2026-08-18 added MPP and the x402 upto scheme, and since 2026-11-19 it also pays AWS Marketplace quotes on the AWS bill.

implementers.name: AWS Marketplace agentic payments (x402 over AWS Billing)
implementers.role: Seller marketplace since 2026-11-19: agents pay x402-enabled Marketplace sellers per request in US dollars through AgentCore payments, billed on the buyer's AWS bill with no crypto wallet. The seller's 402 offers exact on AWS's own aws:base network with asset iso4217:USD, payTo set to the product ID and a seller-signed quote token; the agent retries with a 5-minute payment token in PAYMENT-SIGNATURE, and nothing settles on chain. Exact only at launch, and one payment must be above $0.00 and at most $10,000.00 (an AgentCore rule). Named sellers: Tavily (AWS blog) and Deepgram (its own sample). aws:base is not part of the x402 specification.

implementers.name: Circle Nanopayments (Circle Gateway)
implementers.role: Gas-free USDC payments from $0.000001 using EIP-3009 inside the x402 flow, batched settlement.

implementers.name: Circle Facilitator Service
implementers.role: Circle's hosted x402 facilitator for sellers, launched 2026-09-16: settles USDC on Arc, Base and Polygon PoS with exact, and with upto since 2026-10-13; Circle pays settlement gas and screens both parties. Settling needs a Circle API key (a keyless trial exists); no price was published on 2026-11-14.

implementers.name: Stripe machine payments preview
implementers.role: Charges agents in USDC on Base through x402 and records each settled payment as a PaymentIntent; open to US businesses outside New York, other countries on request (2026-10-19).

implementers.name: Coinbase Agentic Wallets
implementers.role: Coinbase-managed agent wallet, used through the awal CLI or Payments MCP, that pays for x402 services; made available on 2026-02-11 per the CDP changelog as read on 2026-10-19. awal 2.12.3 (2026-11-20) ships a notice that Payments MCP and Agentic Wallet are being retired in favor of Coinbase Wallet MCP, a different wallet, and a withdraw-only phase that would disable x402 payments; the flag endpoint the CLI reads answered 404 on 2026-11-21, so the notice was not active. The former docs redirect to Wallet MCP, and the CDP changelog has no retirement entry.

implementers.name: Coinbase Wallet MCP and Coinbase for Agents
implementers.role: The agent payment options in CDP's agentic accounts docs (read 2026-11-21). Wallet MCP pays x402 in approval mode, where the user signs each prepared action through an approval link, or, for eligible connections, in agent-wallet mode, where a dedicated wallet with an expiring signing grant pays within a saved US dollar budget over a rolling 24-hour window. Its x402 table lists exact and upto on Base, Polygon and Arbitrum, auth-capture on Base mainnet, batch-settlement on those three networks for eligible autonomous sessions, and Solana payments in USDC or USDT in agent-wallet mode only. Coinbase for Agents connects an agent to a Coinbase account through a remote MCP server or a local CLI.

implementers.name: Brave Search API x402 proxy
implementers.role: Seller: since 2026-11-12 Brave sells Brave Search API requests (LLM Context, web, news, images, videos, local) at $0.005 each over x402 V2 exact, USDC on Base (eip155:8453), through a facilitator Brave runs, with no account or API key. Other networks and stablecoins are announced only.

implementers.name: Pay.sh (Solana Foundation)
implementers.role: The pay CLI (MIT, solana-foundation/pay) handles HTTP 402 payments over x402 and MPP. Decrypt and The Block reported on 2026-05-05 that the Solana Foundation and Google Cloud launched Pay.sh, a gateway through which agents pay per request in stablecoins on Solana, with Gemini and BigQuery among the Google Cloud services; that collaboration is reported only, since the Solana Foundation's post could not be read and pay.sh does not mention Google Cloud.

implementers.name: x402scan (Merit Systems)
implementers.role: Explorer, registry and public API for x402 activity.

implementers.name: Google a2a-x402 and AP2 samples
implementers.role: A2A extension and human-present and human-not-present x402 samples.

sdks.name: @x402/core
sdks.note: V2 core types, client and resource server. Versions in this list as of 2026-11-21 (2.32.0 published 2026-11-20); 2.29.0 (2026-10-28) shipped the HEAD-request fix. No SDK implemented the Lightning (lnbtc) binding on that date.

sdks.name: @x402/evm
sdks.note: 2.32.0 (2026-11-20) carries the fix for the batch-settlement voucher advisory GHSA-5cgh-j82v-jvrj (affected 2.12.0 to 2.31.0) and reports a recipient mismatch with the spec code.

sdks.name: @x402/paywall
sdks.note: Browser paywall for humans. A reflected script-injection flaw was fixed in 2.29.0 (2026-10-28) without an advisory.

sdks.name: x402
sdks.note: Legacy V1 package (unscoped); x402-axios, x402-express, x402-fetch, x402-hono and x402-next are V1 too. Deprecated: the READMEs promise security patches only, but x402, x402-express and x402-hono have had no release since 2026-04-16 (x402-axios last released 1.2.1 on 2026-05-29), and the HEAD fix, the paywall script-injection fix and a fix for the open parameterized-route bypass (issue #3850) were all unreleased for V1 on 2026-11-21.

sdks.name: x402
sdks.note: V2 Python SDK, not legacy (2.29.0 published 2026-11-20). Extras include httpx, requests, fastapi, flask, evm, svm, tvm, cardano, mcp and extensions.

sdks.name: github.com/x402-foundation/x402/go/v2
sdks.note: Requires Go 1.26.10 since v2.29.0 (v2.28.0 needed Go 1.24); covers evm, svm and casper.

sdks.name: Java module (java/)
sdks.note: In the repository; no published artifact found.

metrics.definition: Stars on the canonical repository (GitHub API, read 2026-11-14; 6,735 on 2026-10-19).
npm registry downloads of the V2 core package in the 30 days from 2026-10-15 to 2026-11-13 (last-month endpoint, read 2026-11-14). The window from 2026-09-17 to 2026-10-16 had 1,437,614.
metrics.caveat: Includes CI installs; the deprecated legacy V1 package x402 had 2,629,833 in the same window (1,910,242 in the previous one).

metrics.definition: Self-reported counter formerly on the x402.org home page, with no date or method on the page. Archived with this same value from 2025-12-14 to 2026-10-24 (Wayback Machine); the home page no longer showed it on 2026-11-14.
metrics.caveat: History only: it never changed, so it was never a live 30-day figure, and it was removed without an announcement. For the 30 days to 2026-11-14 x402scan showed about 4.93M transactions; agenteconomy.to counted about 5.09M for October 2026. A Base study measured about 145,500 settlements a day from January to June 2026.

metrics.definition: Self-reported counter formerly on the x402.org home page, with no date or method on the page. Archived with this same value from 2025-12-14 to 2026-10-24 (Wayback Machine); the home page no longer showed it on 2026-11-14.
metrics.caveat: History only: it never changed, so it was never a live 30-day figure. For the 30 days to 2026-11-14 x402scan showed about $1.89M; agenteconomy.to counted about $274,000 for October 2026. In March 2026 a16z put a 30-day window at about $3M on chain and $1.6M after removing wash trades.

metrics.definition: Cumulative from the May 2025 launch to 2026-04-21, excluding identified wash and test activity (Artemis's proprietary method); about $0.14 per transaction. Raw totals were over $135.7M across 178.3M transactions.
metrics.caveat: Report commissioned by Visa. On 2026-07-16 The Defiant reported Visa's Cuy Sheffield citing about $19M across about 134M adjusted transactions, with no data date.

metrics.metric: Share of transactions flagged as gamed (Artemis)
metrics.definition: Average share of x402 transactions Artemis flagged as gamed between 2025-11-09 and 2026-02-07 (peak 90.21 percent), reported by Four Pillars. A separate Base study (2025-09-17 to 2026-06-23, different method) classes 21.20 percent of settlements as fictitious and 63.78 percent as internal to linked clusters.
metrics.caveat: Secondary report of Artemis data; the detection logic is not published.

metrics.definition: x402 settlements on Base from 2025-09-17 to 2026-06-23 (280 days), counted in arXiv:2607.12575 (submitted 2026-07-14).
metrics.caveat: The paper argues settlement counts are not adoption because they can be manufactured almost for free.

metrics.definition: Claim in the V2 launch post.
metrics.caveat: Raw self-reported count. Visa and Artemis counted about 38M adjusted transactions in November 2025 and 109.6M adjusted (178.3M raw) from launch to 2026-04-21.

metrics.definition: Quote from Rishin Sharma (Solana Foundation) in the Linux Foundation release of 2026-04-02, for 2026 to date; a self-reported figure from an interested party.
metrics.caveat: Crypto Briefing reported about 70 percent of monthly volume for mid August 2026. Visa and Artemis data (adjusted, cumulative to 2026-04-21) put Base at about 90 percent of transactions and 93 percent of volume; the windows differ.

metrics.definition: Past 30 Days view of x402scan's overall stats, read 2026-11-14 (window from 2026-10-15); the same view showed about $1.89M in volume, 31.6K buyers and 14.4K sellers. On 2026-10-19 it showed 3.02M transactions and $1.23M.
metrics.caveat: x402scan's own indexing of facilitator settlements; trackers count differently. agenteconomy.to's monthly series gives about 5.09M transactions but only about $274,000 for October 2026.

metrics.metric: Cumulative x402 transactions settled on chain (agenteconomy.to)
metrics.definition: 200,193,219 transactions and $42,967,916 of stablecoin volume across 12 chains and 18 tracked facilitators, measured from public on-chain settlement data (read 2026-11-14).
metrics.caveat: Counts settlements from the facilitators it tracks, not proven commerce. Its October 2026 value (about $274,000) is far below x402scan's 30-day volume (about $1.89M to 2026-11-14); the methods differ.

metrics.definition: Range across unnamed trackers reported by Crypto Briefing on 2026-09-15.
metrics.caveat: Trackers count differently: x402scan showed 234.69M all-time transactions on 2026-10-19, Chainalysis reported more than 138 million x402 transactions on Base by the end of its 2026 report period (2026-10-14), and agenteconomy.to counted about 200.2M cumulative transactions as of 2026-11-14.

metrics.definition: Organizations listed on x402.org/members: 19 Premier, 26 General and 13 Associate (57 on 2026-10-19).
metrics.caveat: 40 at the 2026-07-14 launch, 17 of them Premier; the Linux Foundation said more than 50 active members on 2026-10-01.

metrics.metric: Lifetime x402 payments (Solana Foundation talk, reported)
metrics.definition: Figure attributed to Rishin Sharma of the Solana Foundation in a Breakpoint 2026 talk in London, as reported by Decrypt and Crypto Briefing on 2026-11-17; counted since the 2025 launch.
metrics.caveat: Self-reported by an interested party and known only from press reports, with no method; about twice agenteconomy.to's cumulative count (about 200.2M transactions and $43.0M as of 2026-11-14).

costs.value: First 1,000 on-chain transactions each month free, then $0.001 per on-chain transaction
costs.caveat: Counts on-chain transactions, not payment requests. CDP began charging on 2026-01-01 after announcing it on 2025-12-01; check the page for current rates.

costs.value: exact and EVM upto: one; Solana upto: two; batch-settlement: one claim covers many vouchers
costs.whoPays: Facilitator pays gas; the seller pays CDP's fee per on-chain transaction
costs.caveat: Deposits, refunds and withdrawals in batch-settlement count as one transaction each.

costs.value: On-chain gas plus 30 percent per settlement since 2026-09-21, paid in $0.001 credits; 1,000 free credits per receiving wallet, for life
costs.caveat: Rates are recomputed daily. On 2026-10-19 a Solana exact settlement cost 1.33 credits and a Base exact (EIP-3009) settlement 2.09, so the free credits covered about 750 or 480 settlements.

costs.value: 0.3 percent of each transaction executed through its facilitator, on all paid plans shown
costs.whoPays: The thirdweb account holder (the seller using its facilitator)
costs.caveat: Plan fees and RPC charges are separate.

costs.value: No facilitator fee; the operator pays gas, RPC, operations and compliance costs
Ethereum L1 about $0.01 on 2026-10-19 ($1 to $5 under normal congestion); Base under $0.005 to $0.01; Solana under $0.001 to $0.005
costs.whoPays: Facilitator on the exact EVM path and as Solana fee payer, or the merchant when it sponsors
costs.caveat: The Ethereum figure is one EIP-3009 USDC transfer measured on 2026-10-19 (81,053 gas at 0.045 gwei, ETH at $2,432). The other ranges are Spark's mid-2026 low and normal congestion estimates; gas prices move by orders of magnitude.

costs.value: Payments from $0.000001 USDC; Circle says batched settlement means neither party pays per-transaction fees
costs.whoPays: Neither party per payment (Circle). The buyer makes a one-time on-chain deposit; moving funds out of Gateway pays a gas fee per burn that varies by source chain, and crosschain transfers add a percentage transfer fee, except to or from Arc
costs.caveat: Circle loads current Gateway fees from its fee API; the $0.01 gas fee and 0.005 percent transfer fee on its fees page are illustrative inputs to a worked example, not a price list. Who pays the gas for batch settlement is not stated.

costs.value: The buyer pays the seller's quoted US dollar price on the AWS bill; the seller pays AWS Marketplace's 3 percent SaaS listing fee
costs.whoPays: Buyer pays the quote; seller pays the listing fee
costs.caveat: No chain and no gas: AgentCore payments issues a payment token, and AWS Marketplace meters the charge, bills it and pays the seller through its disbursements. One AWS Billing payment must be above $0.00 and at most $10,000.00 (an AgentCore rule); refunds are billing adjustments on invoices.

costs.value: No charge beyond standard AWS WAF pricing; AWS takes no fee on content revenue
costs.whoPays: The publisher pays standard AWS WAF charges
costs.caveat: Settlement runs through Coinbase Developer Platform's x402 facilitator, and AWS's posts do not say whether facilitator fees apply. Payouts go to the publisher's own wallet.
x402 itself charges nothing; costs are facilitator fees and gas. cloudflare:402 is credit billed by Cloudflare as merchant of record under its own terms.
